newsitem.title: GERMANY: DIHT says don't dither on euro/millennium plans.
newsitem.headline: DIHT says don't dither on euro/millennium plans.

text.p: German firms cannot afford to dither in preparing their computer systems for the transition to the single European currency and the "millennium bug", the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) said on Monday.
The January 1999 start of European monetary union (EMU) and the turn of the century present huge and nearly concurrent challenges for software designers, suppliers and users, DIHT said.
"In data processing it would make sense to combine the preparations for the euro with the millennium change," DIHT said, based on a survey of 800 computer-user firms and 130 software houses.
"Doubts about 'if' EMU will come must end, education about 'how' must be intensified," it said, as part of an action plan proposed to the European Commission.
DIHT urged all to assume that EMU would start on schedule on January 1, 1999, and to start their preparations right away, if they haven't done so already.
Smaller companies face bigger problems with the two transitions, and will need more outside assistance.
Companies should see the needed measures as an opportunity to reorganise and upgrade their computer systems, but too many are focusing on adapting existing systems, it said.
